subject: Simulation dies when capacity drops to zero

messages.author: 0978dc43df44152e
messages.subject: Simulation dies when capacity drops to zero
parts:
I’m simulating a service with fixed hours that closes at 6pm, and using the schedule function to adjust staffing over a 24-hour period. There is zero staff between the hours of 6pm and 8am the following morning.


     engineer_schedule <- schedule(c(480, 600, 960, 1080), c(4, 8, 4, 0), period = 1440)

 

The simulation runs okay until time 1080 is reached when the capacity drops to zero.

 

 

   1070.06 |   arrival: assisted customer26|  activity: Leave          | function()

   1070.06 |   arrival: assisted customer26|  activity: Timeout        | function()

   1077.15 |   arrival: assisted customer26|  activity: Seize          | [], 1

   1077.15 |  resource: Tom            |   arrival: assisted customer26| SERVE

   1077.15 |   arrival: assisted customer26|  activity: Rollback       | Timeout

      1080 |   manager: Jason          | parameter: capacity       | 0

      1080 |  resource: Jason          |   arrival: community question2| PREEMPT

      1080 |   manager: William        | parameter: capacity       | 0

      1080 |  resource: William        |   arrival: assisted customer25| PREEMPT

      1080 |  resource: William        |   arrival: chat customer9 | PREEMPT

      1080 |   manager: Tom            | parameter: capacity       | 0

 

The session then pauses for about 2 minutes followed by a message that R encountered a fatal error, and the session aborts.


Is there a better way to do this? I'd like to quiesce the service at the end of the day and pick it up the following morning and measure the service time in days.

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Re: Simulation dies when capacity drops to zero
parts:
Hi, this test case summarises the problem, and it’s already solved in the master repo. But please note that you are doing the following in your code:

create_trajectory("research/analyze") %>%
  # agent does research but will need more information from customer
  # do the research and send customer the request for information
  timeout(function() rexp(1, 0.0333)) %>%
  release_selected(amount = 1) %>%
  # if issue is resolved, leave, otherwise wait for customer
  leave(prob = function() sample(0:1, 1, FALSE, c(0.3, 0.7))) %>%
  # engineer is now free but case is not yet resolved - wait for customer to respond
  timeout(function() rexp(1, 0.1666) ) %>%
  seize_selected(amount = 1) %>%
  # customer just responded. Must review the case.
  # seize the engineer and rollback the trajectory
  rollback(amount = 5)

I don’t know if this is intended or not, but note that, after one rollback, the arrival leaves this trajectory without releasing a resource. I always wanted this to be a feature, but now I see that is a source of possible problems. Therefore, this situation now still works, but a warning is displayed showing the resources that were not released (see #76).

If you don’t want this, simply put a release_selected(1) after that rollback. Please also note that, since recent versions, you cannot specify priority and preemptible in a seize: you need to move these arguments to add_generator.

Regards,
Iñaki

​
